txt: As you approach, the man turns and greets you with a polite wave.
He nods. "Anything else?"

He pats his pockets. "But, oh! I don't have my leaflets on me today. That's too bad. You can always call our information line. Making information available is part of the Moralintern's commitment to transparency."
He smiles. "You could say I'm undoing some of the *material* damage the international community caused when we arrived here."
The awkward silence that follows is yours to fill.
The man considers your words a moment, then nods slowly...
The man frowns. "Well, under ordinary circumstances, the Committee contacts *you*."
The man gives the lieutenant a nervous look.
The man looks at you expectantly.
The man nods. "It's the responsibility of any good welfare state to take care of its most unfortunate citizens."
The man nods. "See? That's the kind of progress that the Moralintern makes possible."
The man nods. "You are a credit to the RCM. If more Revacholians were like you, they might be part of EPIS by now."
The man seems slightly relieved, as though he's just narrowly survived a perilous bend in the road.
The man sees you approaching and turns away...
The man shakes his head solemnly. "A great shame, yes. Colonialism is a dark spectre in Oranje's past..."
The man sighs. "I only pray that the ICP apprehends this fugitive before more corporate secrets are lost..."
The man takes a deep breath. "Yes, there's nothing like a stroll along the coast to lift one's spirits."
The man wipes his glasses. "You're right, of course. That is what one is supposed to do in such circumstances. I was simply in shock..."
When you turn back the man is looking at you expectantly.
With that, he turns his back to you once more.
"*Extremely* tenuous..."
"*Précisément*! Too much inflation, bread becomes too expensive; too much deflation, it becomes too cheap for bakers to produce..."
"*Thousands* of corporate secrets may be at stake here. I shudder to think what damage that might do to the international markets..."
"*Transparence* has always been our highest priority."
"...which is *why* the work of the Moralintern is so critical. It is our great bulwark against another century of bloodshed."
"A *fugitive*?"
"A *politicien* is never off z'e clock."
"A cafeteria manager, you say? How strange. Normally fugitives don't take on such *public* roles."
"A drug-addled *spy-ring*! That sounds rather *strange*, don't you think?"
"A moment, officer."
"A rather *brutal* perspective on history." He frowns slightly. "I personally take the more nuanced view that it was regrettably harsh, but perhaps necessary to end the war..."
"A sound monetary policy is *essential* for addressing *uncertainty*. Stability is the *raison d'être* of the Moralintern. It's the reason why I identify as a moralist."
"A supranational political alliance, the United States of Occident."
"A very moralist answer," the man nods.
"A what... a *child*?" He seems confused at first, then disappointed.
"About what?"
"Ah, a very useful gift for a police detective, I'm sure. Fascinating, *how much history* is contained right here, if only one knows where to look for it..."
"Ah, bon? I'm all ears, officer."
"Ah, good to hear. Excellent. On behalf of the Moralintern, let me thank you for this service..."
"Ah, he was a soldier?"
"Ah, is that what those pock marks are? I might've guessed. Fascinating, *how much history* is contained right here, if only one knows where to look for it..."
"Ah, look! A seagull."
"Ah, my friend, but the lesson of the Revolution is that communism does not work."

"Ah, my friend. My friend is a good young man. His family immigrated here from Kedra and life has not been easy for him. But he understands the importance of education. He has taken his future into his own hands and that's all that matters."
"Ah, of course. Carry on then."
"Ah, super, here you are again, officer. How can I help?"
"Ah, super, it's the officer! I was not expecting to run into you again, but things have a funny way of turning out, no?"
"Ah, that's right. You did say this was all just a *hypothetical* scenario..."
"Ah, very good, then." Your remark seems to have completely vanished from his mind.
"Ah, well, I'm glad to hear that at least. It would really be *quite unusual* for you to have never noticed it before..."

"Ah, well, I'm renovating it. It is an interesting project. The building used to be a twelve-story skyscraper before the cannons took the top four stories off. This of course happened when the Coalition forces landed here..."
"Ah, well. Burglary is a serious violation of the right to property, but it is a *local* matter. Thus, the Moralintern need not get involved."
"Ah, yes, the unattainable ideal. Never settle for less! Good luck with that, my friend."
"Aha, a *condottiere*," the man says, as though describing a character from a fantasy novel. "Yes, it's hard to believe they still exist."
"Aha," he says, his voice suddenly cool. "A *nationalist*, I see. In other circumstances I might be compelled to report you for *sedition*..."
"All I can say is that it was late."
"All men, I presume. But again, I couldn't see very clearly."
"All of z'is is perfectly normal. A bit mundane if anything."
"Already leaving?" He shakes his head merrily. "À tout à l'heure, officer!"
"Already?" He glances at his watch. "Well, I'm glad I could help."
"Always my pleasure to be of assistance to the RCM. Godspeed, and if we don't meet again, bonne chance!"
"And listening! It has the most objective vantage point in the entire city. Not to mention a vast array of radio, photographic, and meteorological monitoring instruments."
"And my friend's not even your typical local -- definitely not just another Martin Martinaise or Raoul Revachol. Maybe that's why we're friends."
"And now, this conversation is over. Good day, *officer*."
"And then, well, I had some extra time on my hands, so I decided to stroll down here. It's quite peaceful, isn't it?"
"And what is that, officer?" He turns to face you.
"And, of course, any loss of life is a tragedy." The man seems to observe a moment of silence. "So tell me, what have you learned about the victim?"
"Are we really so bad for wanting compromise, peace, and prosperity -- on reasonable, achievable terms? Ask yourself that."
"As I said, the loss of any life is terrible, no matter who the person may have been..."
"As a common lorry driver, you say? Interesting. Are you sure?"

"As founding members they are *both* very EPIS. Oranje carries a lot of political weight, while Sur-la-Clef takes care of the business side of things -- Sur-la-Clef hosts the headquarters of the major EPIS institutions."
"Au contraire. It's how millions of people end up where they are, meeting the people they meet. It's how I came here, and my friend, too."
"Because I *did it*?" the man scoffs.
"Because a great percentage of Revachol's culture hails from Sur-la-Clef -- its language, its people, its cuisine even, or at least in the downtown La Delta area."
"Because moralists believe in a normal, stable world governed by democratic values."
"Besides, in certain less-advanced nations the Moralintern may defer to local custom..."
"But I suspect you knew that already. I can't say I'm surprised. The fine reputation of the men and women serving in the RCM is well deserved."
"But I told you, officer. He's a bright young man here to pursue his education. Education is the foundation of our future, especially the arts. It is a cornerstone of our civilization."
"But if you have information of a vital interest, they might be willing to entertain an exception. In which case, I would advise you to contact them via Coalition Warship Archer."

"But in that case, you would require a radio transmitter capable of broadcasting on Coalition frequencies. And that kind of technology naturally isn't typically available for non-Coalition use. Yes, it *is* a bit of a conundrum."
"But not *too* far below, no. Too below is also bad -- below, *but close to* 2%."
"But now that I start to think of it, it was for an improv class anyway. It's this funny theatre thing, you know," he moves his fingers, "very *creative*, helps relieve stress."
"But of course!"

"But rest assured: The Oranjese government has committed to producing a timetable that would lay out a path to transition to a professional army. Soon there'll be no need for mercenaries like this poor man."
"But the million reál view stays. You can't take that away." He knocks on the balcony door, his face mirrored in the darkened glass.
"But they are working towards it! You're all doing very well here, relatively speaking." He gives you an approving nod.
"But we were talking about my friend here, not politics..." He chuckles gently.

"Corporate espionage may technically be legal in *Revachol*, but elsewhere it's a very high-level offence. It violates a number of international agreements, in particular the First La Cherte Accord..."
"Corpse desecration is morally repugnant, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"Debating. You should consider joining a debating society for adults. I hear they're *oodles* of fun. I used to have a flyer for one, but..."
"Do you have everything you need from me? I'm afraid we won't have the chance to speak again once you leave."
"Do you think *peace* is boring? What about *prosperity*?"
"Does this behaviour represent the RCM's *official stance* toward its Coalition partners?" He turns to the lieutenant.
"Drummers? Why... no... but then, I don't know what a drummer is *supposed* to look like."

"EPIS is a very special program developed by the Moralintern to support certain Occidental nations. It began as a unified system of weights and measures, which proved to be a *wild* success. Nothing but kilograms and centimetres as far as the eye can see!"
"Ellis Kortenaer? That's an interesting name."
"Especially from a common officer of the Revachol Citizens Militia."
"Even high-ranking bureaucrats are entitled to a holiday."
"Eventually their shouts died down, and that was all. There were no gunshots, no celebratory shouts, no anything."
"Every one of us has our role to play."
"Everyone needs to share z'e *responsabilité*."
"Evrart Claire? Surely you're mistaken."
"Exactly. *I* don't find it boring, I find it *fulfilling*. Peace is what allows me to have my morning coffee, my afternoon golf, my sundown friends."
"Extremely distasteful behaviour. I cannot condone either drug use or needless boasting..."
"Fascinating. I always thought it was more like a dragonfly. But isn't it interesting how humanity always finds inspiration in nature?"
"First responsabilité, then stabilité, then prospérité!"
"Governmental issues take me all over Revachol as you can see."
"He's a bright young man here to pursue his education. Education is the foundation of our future, especially the arts. It is a cornerstone of our civilization."
"He's a truly free spirit. He likes all the arts. Perhaps graphic design? Printmaking? Who knows? The world is open wide for a talented youth like him."
"He's deeply enmeshed in the study of the fine arts, yes."
"He... so you spoke with the victim *before* he died?"
"Hmmm, that could be *quite* bad, depending on what sort of place you're talking about."

"Hmmm, this is quite the problem, very tricky. Of course, the Archer has orders to fire on any unidentified aerostatics that might approach it, so it might be safer to get in touch *from the ground*..."

"How did any of us become friends? Bad things happening on the Insulindian isola. Oil platforms ablaze in the night. Civil wars lasting for years. Finally, the international community is forced to step in."
"I *have*. The only thing Evrart is a fugitive from is the *exercise machine*..."
"I accept your apology, officer, out of my *profound* respect for the RCM, and the importance of our continuing partnership."
"I agree. And we as an international community should strive to bring this prosperity to every kid on every isola."
"I believe they were mostly white, though I believe I saw two Areopagites among them. And I am quite certain that one spoke with a Mesque accent."
"I couldn't see their faces well, and there were quite a few of them. But they were very loud and very... Martinaise..." He pauses, looking for the right wording.
"I couldn't tell you exactly. Less than ten. Maybe eight?"
"I do hope you're able to bring his killer or killers to justice. We must show that the rule of law still applies... even in Revachol."
"I don't mean to discourage you, of course, just to say that it won't be *easy* to reach the Committee."
"I don't z'ink conclusions should be rushed at z'is point."
"I find it a great comfort to know there are benevolent powers watching over all, in strict accordance with the Wayfarer Act and the Bristelmüne Conventions."

"I got it from the head of the Samaran delegation on my trip to Lo-Manthang. It's made from a *special* charcoal-coloured bamboo. It's an emblem of the formal normalization of our diplomatic relations."
"I have nothing to say to you. Get out of my sight."
"I heard you talking to my friend outside... Very good. Super. I am here to assist you in any way possible. Ask me about the hanging."
"I must admit. I did not take you for a sightseer. What do you want now?"
"I suggest you work on your *investigative skills* a bit more before you go around accusing children of crimes."
"I suppose there might be some way to *circuit-bend* your way onto those frequencies, but you'd have to be one of those *techno-tinkerers* to do it."
"I understand that you're here to investigate a *murder*," the man says, his face grave, "but I must impress upon you the *seriousness* of this matter..."
"I was on the balcony when it happened, getting some fresh air. I remember that first they came in, carrying what looked like a body, and then I saw all the surrounding windows go dead one-by-one..."
"I went back inside."
"I won't stand for this." His left eye starts twitching -- as the last warning. "What's your name? I'll have your badge!"
"I would offer to connect you with the committee myself, but alas, I am not actually *in* Martinaise."
"I'll be sure I make a note of your contributions in my report. Revachol is fortunate to have police officers like you."
"I'll make note of your claims in my report, but I'm sorry to say it's likely to end up in the back of a filing cabinet somewhere in Mirova, unread and forgotten."
"I'm afraid I don't have anything else to add."
"I'm afraid I must *insist* that you tell me what you know. Or I'll be forced to make a *very* unfavourable report to my superiors at the Moralintern."
"I'm all ears, officer."
"I'm just enjoying the view," the man smiles, nodding to the window.
"I'm listening." He turns to face you.
"I'm sorry I couldn't be of more assistance."
"I'm sorry to say I did, officer." The man gives a solemn nod.
"I'm sure you'll see him around, he's very active."
"I... see. Well, you must be a very thorough detective. So what else did you learn?"
"If *stabilité* is ensured, progress will naturally follow."
"If we can ensure *stabilité*, progress will naturally follow."
"In a *wider* sense z'is is actually my apartment. And yours."

"Interesting. In a sense, that's the very idea. The Coalition doesn't want the people of Revachol to feel that they are under a *military* occupation. That is why the Archer is always careful to maintain a constant, discreet distance."
"Is that an RCM *term of art* for the *wrongfully accused*?"
"Is that so? Have you come to *enforce* an arrest warrant?"
"Is this 'Option D' usually the most *reasonable* answer?"
"Isn't it? A triumph of both technical ingenuity and international cooperation. I, for one, feel much safer knowing it's up there, watching all of us."
"It is ze most important thing."

"It was *such* a wild success that we expanded it into an economic union for the processing of steel -- another success. And between you and me... the Moralintern feels *emboldened* by this success. Emboldened to take EPIS to the next level."

"It's against diplomatic best practices for an official in my position to be discussing murders with local militiamen." He pauses. "And I'm pressed for time. After you leave, I should be leaving as well."
"It's been such a wild, *extraordinary* success thus far. We are very excited to take it to the next level..."
"It's moving towards the right direction and that's all that matters. Progress is measured in centimetres, my friend."
"It's one day going to be a *candidate member* of EPIS, sure."
"It's possible, officer, but I cannot say with certainty. It was very dark, you must remember."

"It's the central goal of any sound monetary policy. Maintaining ze price stabilité is essential to maintaining high levels of economic activity, which is essential for maintaining high levels of employment..."
"It's the international organization for moralists. Hence 'Moralist International.' The Institute of Price Stability is just one of its many *mind babies* -- as is the Coalition."
"It's warm," he nods. "It's also known for its mandarin trees and dust storms from Supramundi."
"Kedra is a candidate member of EPIS. But, between you and me, their potential membership is a more... *contentious* issue."
"Kedra's an emerging market, but it still has a long way to go -- maybe that's why my friend's ménage decided to emigrate."
"La communauté internationale is what Revacholians colloquially call *the Coalition*. In other words, the nations that stopped the disaster of the Revolution."
"Lely? That's an interesting name."
"Let me just say that I have *complete confidence* in the RCM. I'm sure you'll figure something out."
"Let's just say that the labouring classes can get rather *expressive* with their profanities."
"Listen," he says, raising his hand...
"Lots of opportunities for revitalisation here."
"Mais que faites-vous, officer?" Your hand bumps up against the man's solid if somewhat fleshy chest.

"Martin Martinaise? That's not a name. Are you referring to my friend? But I told you, he's from Kedra -- definitely not just another Martin Martinaise or Raoul Revachol. Perhaps that's why he and I became friends..."
"Martinaise? No, Martinaise is... something else."

"Mm, well that's très simple. I was visiting the fishing village just north of here. They have applied for a series of micro-loans to revitalise the old market, and well, I wished to see the situation *first-hand*..."
"Moderacy in everything -- even in moderacy."
"Moralism is all about compromise and achieving the achievable. It's pragmatic, realistic, and level-headed, an ideology for *doers*. Are you a doer, my friend? It looks to me like you are."
"Moreover, it is a great sponsor of less-emerged countries. Revachol is only one of its many darlings whose progress it supports and cherishes."
"Much as I'm inclined to believe you, I'm not sure my colleagues at the ICP will..."
"My friend comes and goes. I'm sure you'll see him around, he's a busy bee."
"My friend, if it's *la responsabilité* you're after, I have good news for you: There's no need to form such a committee, because it already exists!"
"My friend, my friend, what about him?"
"My friend, that is only because you have never known the *alternative*. And I pray you never do."
"My name is Charles Villedrouin and I'm an official with the Coalition Government. I work for the Institute of Price Stabilité, on assignment from Sur-la-Clef."
"My watch..." He looks at his watch, as though noticing it for the first time. "Yes, now I remember -- it was thirty minutes past midnight, give or take."
"No, *listen*," he says again, looking outside...
"No, I didn't see the corpse until the following day."
"No, no, candidate members *do* become members, why do we even have the whole system in place if they don't? It just takes time -- time and evaluation."
"No, no, don't be silly. We're simply speaking in an informal capacity. *Officially* I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
"No, no, no. Evrart would have no need to dirty his hands in such a way..."
"No, no." The man shakes his head. "I mean it was so strange I could barely believe what was happening..."
"None of z'is is weird."
"Not boring, my friend. *Responsible*."
"Now that that's settled, was there anything else you'd like to discuss?"
"Now, enough of this delightful political interlude. Was there anything else you wanted to ask?"
"Now, now. Human life is *always* more important than private property..."
"Now, was there anything else you wanted to discuss?"
"Now, was there anything else you wished to discuss?"
"Now, was there something else you wanted to discuss?"
"Now, what brings you down to the coast?"
"Of course, I'm glad I could help."
"Of course, I'm sorry I couldn't be the 'break' you were looking for. Good luck with the investigation."
"Of course, anything I can do to assist the RCM."
"Of course, we are speaking informally, but *officially* I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
"Of course. Let me just say it has been an emotional week for me." He forms a little rooftop with his fingers. Cold air comes in from the balcony.
"Officer, it's very difficult to describe what I saw that night. It was so surreal to me, like in a play."
"Officer, please! The Moralintern is dedicated to fostering a more tolerant and pluralistic society. There's no room for racial slurs there."
"Officer, the yard was pitch black. There was nothing to see. But I could still hear their voices. They were threatening to kill that poor man."
"Officer, you have to understand... I can't give you his personal information. I'm sure you have your own methods and databases, right? Please don't put me in this situation."
"Officer, you shouldn't speak ill of the dead!"
"Officer..."
"Officer? You mean to say you haven't noticed the giant Coalition aerostatic peacefully patrolling the skies over Revachol?"
"Officers of the Revachol Citizens Militia." The man in business-casual removes his cuff links.

"Oh yes, my friend has a great eye for these things. He refuses to tell me where it came from -- it's a mystery. Hehehe." He smiles. "I believe they call this type of frame *industrial*. It's very comfy."
"Oh! Hahaha. A good joke. Very funny. Littering is of course a local offence that need not concern the Moralintern."
"Oh! How wonderful. I've heard it's *oodles* of fun. Not that I have time to take up new hobbies myself..."
"Oh, it's hard to put an exact date on it. I believe the proposal for the timetable is due to be completed around '60 or '61."

"Oh, it's very urban and very well-organized. Their streets are clean, their horsecars run on time, the people are polite and efficient. Like I said, they are an example for less-emerged nations to follow."
"Oh, we got it from an atelier in the East Delta Commerce Centre. Personally I think it's a little culturally insensitive, but the material is great. Sadly the shop is now out of business..."
"Oh, yes, the big bad Coalition crushed the Revolution. Tell me, if the revolution was succeeding, would it have been crushed so easily?"
"Oh, yes. Sur-la-Clef is *mega-benevolent* to its darlings."
"Oh? That's unusual. The Oranjese are not the kind of people you associate with heinous crimes. It's such an upstanding and responsible country..."

"One of the wonders of democracy is that everyone is allowed to have his own opinion." The man pats his pockets, looking for something. "And not just allowed, *encouraged* even. Have you ever tried debate?"

"Only that there were about eight or ten -- I couldn't make out anything, it was so dark -- and that it was *quiet*," he says, smoothing his hair. "Quietest lynching I ever *heard of*, let alone heard..."

"Oranje is an *exemplary* nation who, as a core member of EPIS, contributes 28% of our annual budget. Next to Sur-la-Clef, Oranje is probably the most prominent member of the international community."

"Oranje's economy is one of the most advanced in the world. It has successfully transitioned from heavy industry to advanced services, and generally acts as an engine for sustainable change in the international community."
"Perhaps he does, perhaps he does not. In any case, this conversation is over. Good day, officers."
"Perhaps your blood sugar is a bit low? As I was saying, *officially* speaking I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
"Précisément. *Officially* I am still in La Delta, preparing for an upcoming conference on fuel oil derivatives..."
"Really?" The man frowns. "*Here*? How can you be sure?"
"Revachol is generally... difficult. It's led by an interim government, which means it hasn't yet achieved *full* democracy..."
"Right. That should be enough for the ICP. Very good. On behalf of the Moralintern, let me thank you for this service..."
"Selling drugs is certainly unfortunate, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"Someone is always watching."
"Sorry, who?" The man throws a quick glance at his watch.
"Sounds like you're a moralist indeed, my friend. Welcome."
"Stealing from misguided pseudo-scientists is unfortunate, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"Suffice it to say, that is *not* how we do things in Sur-la-Clef."
"Sure, go ahead, it's a beautiful space." He glances at his watch. "Let me know if you have any further questions."
"Take your daily bread, *par example*. Too much inflation, bread becomes too expensive; too much deflation, it becomes too cheap for bakers to produce..."
"Thankfully, the region is becoming more and more stable. I'm confident that atrocities like this belong in the past. The future is..." he snaps his fingers, "*tranquilou bilou!*"
"That is *extremely serious*!"
"That is certainly a *euphemistic* way to describe what I recall..."
"That is extremely unfortunate. Yes, it's regrettable that this practice has a history in certain Occidental nations, even highly advanced members of EPIS..."

"That is part of the idea, of course. The Coalition doesn't want the people of Revachol to feel that they are under a *military* occupation. That is why the Archer is always careful to maintain a constant, discreet distance."
"That it's never going to happen. They entered negotiations in '21 and it's been pending ever since."
"That's a giant you're describing. No, they were all *quite* human, so far as I could tell."

"That's one way to put it, yes. They certainly have the power to exert influence over others, but they only do it in the name of regional stability. After all, Oranje is a Moralintern nation, not some crazed Mesque petro-fascist state."
"That's really all I can tell you about it." He forms a little rooftop with his fingers. Cold air sweeps in from the balcony.
"That's when I understood -- I should not be seeing this."
"That's why it would be extremely irregular, or potentially even *inappropriate* for me to intercede with the Committee concerning a district I'm not officially in."
"That's why the Institute of Price Stabilité works to keep inflation just below 2%..."
"That, my friend, is your responsabilité. I cannot take it from you, nor can you delegate it to someone else..."
"The Coalition believes in the importance of informing the public about the benefits of ze price stabilité. Transparency is one of our principles. Would you like an informational pamphlet?"

"The Coalition is only looking out for *ze price stabilité*." He raises an index finger. "Inflation is a killer, like a heart disease blocking the normal circulation of the economy -- It must be controlled..."

"The Comité de Responsabilité de Revachol. It acts as a sort-of clearinghouse for Coalition activities. To put it simply, they are the ultimate arbiters of la responsabilité in this part of the world."
"The Insulindian Bay."
"The Occident is part of the normal world. Oranje, Sur-la-Clef..."
"The economy impacts the entire *international community*, which is why it requires international oversight."
"The sea air is so invigorating, don't you agree?"
"There's no way I can submit this report to the ICP -- they'd have my head examined!"
"They gave him a successful *career*." The man holds up a finger as though he's made a brilliant point.
"This fugitive must be turned over to the ICP immediately. Have you apprehended them already?"
"This is a great relief. The sanctity of corporate secrets is a cornerstone of the international order..."
"This is quite the problem, very tricky. Of course, the Archer has orders to fire on any unidentified aerostatics that might approach it, so it might be safer to get in touch *from the ground*..."

"This place used to be a luxury accommodation, before the Revolution. Apartments, of course, were much bigger then -- a few walls have been added here and there, leaving some of the tenants without a private bathroom or a kitchen..."
"This whole area is a strong candidate for a micro-loan."
"Those funny... Oh." He blinks. "Officer, that kind of language is unbecoming of an officer of the RCM..."
"Though, I do hope whoever was responsible at least compensated the building's owner appropriately."
"Tsk-tsk. Racial slurs certainly have no place in a pluralistic society, but what does that have to do with corporate espionage?"
"Unauthorised circuit-bending is a very serious matter with grave security implications, but as of the moment there is no specific law *forbidding* it, in Revachol at least..."
"Unbelievable. I have never seen the nerve before..."
"Unfortunately not, no, I don't have the pleasure. I am merely a representative of the Coalition Government, not very well-versed in technology. But you..."
"Unfortunately not, no, I don't have the pleasure. I am merely a representative of the Coalition Government, not very well-versed in technology..."
"Very good. Now was there anything else you'd like to discuss?"
"Very good. What else then?"
"Very well, *Harry*. You're a disgrace to the RCM. Get out of my sight, this instant!" He points at the door.
"Very well, *Mr. Du Bois*. You're a disgrace to the RCM. Get out, this instant!" He points at the door.
"Was there anything else?"
"We're old friends, nothing's taboo between us. He comes and goes."
"Well certainly one cannot rely simply on generalizations -- that would go against our commitment to individual freedoms..."
"Well said. Let us just be grateful that *we* don't live in such fascinating times."
"Well, I can certainly understand *that*." The man loosens his tie knot and appears to relax slightly. "That hanging was a surreal play. Everything since then has been too..."
"Well, I would say that is very bad, indeed. Not super."
"Well, do you value freedom? Do you believe in a normal, stable world governed by democratic values?"
"Well, no matter. I should thank you for bringing this to our attention. Your efforts have been noted."
"Well, no matter. You've done the Moralintern a great service regardless of your *personal* views..."
"Well, of course it *is* a heavily armed and armoured warship with a full complement. But I assure you its purpose in Revachol is to *keep* the peace, not disturb it."
